transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-11-21
Start: 15:00 PT | Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Rita Gomez (Redwood CSM); Priya Nair (Sandstone Head of ML), Tom Vargas (Sandstone VP Eng), Evan Li (Infra), Ally Brooks (Security)

--- Summary (auto) ---
Quick recap of hosting options (hosted/dedicated/private) and three primary decision axes: latency & SLOs, cost/burn, and compliance/privacy. Agreed to 6-week POC with benchmarks in week1-2, decision at mid-December.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick roll call, we can kick off — I think the main agenda is to scope the POC so you can pick a hosting mode. Marcus will lead the benchmark talk.
[00:12] Priya: Yep, hi all — Priya here. We're mostly looking to replace our current embedding + rerank pipeline for search and a few chat flows. Cost is a big leaver for us but latency/user experience is critical for search.
[00:23] Tom: Hey, Tom — we also have a compliance box; some docs can't leave our VPC and we need audit logs. So, the decision isn't purely perf/cost.
[00:30] Marcus: Got it. I'll talk through the plan then we can map to hosted/dedicated/private tradeoffs. First, what are your rough traffic shapes? QPS, message size, concurrency?
[00:40] Evan: Typical ingest is bursty — 200 qps in morning peak for search, averages about 35 qps across the day. Median prompt length is ~60 tokens, worst-case 450 tokens for some long context chat. We expect ~10M tokens/day at peak months.
[00:55] Marcus: Good. For planning that's helpful. Are you expecting steady concurrency or lots of short bursts?
[01:04] Priya: Short bursts mostly, we use client-side batching in the app but still see spikes. Also we have a nightly bulk rerank job that runs 2x/day with larger batches.
[01:16] Lena: To make this concrete, what are your success criteria? Like p50/p95 latency targets, uptime, and cost constraints?
[01:24] Priya: P50 < 80ms, p95 < 250ms for search queries. Availability 99.9% in production. Cost: we'd like to keep annual inference spend under $150k for this product line; pilot should remain below $20k.
[01:40] Marcus: Great — that gives us clear SLOs. For those latency numbers, hosted mode often hits lower ops time-to-value since we can route to high-throughput kernels. But for strict data residency and audit logs, Private or Dedicated in a VPC are options.
[01:55] Tom: If we did dedicated, what's the committed GPU footprint we'd need for your target qps?
[02:04] Marcus: Rough ballpark: for 200 qps with mixed sequences, if you go with a standard 16k context medium model and quantized variant, you'd be looking at a dedicated pool of roughly 4 x A100-equivalent cards (this is very rough). That maps to cost estimates we'll share. For hosted, we'd simulate with continuous batching and caching; actual cost may be 20-40% lower due to multi-tenancy optimizations and prefix KV caching.
[02:26] Evan: When you say KV caching, do you mean session state caching? We can't leak anything across tenants.
[02:32] Marcus: Right, KV cache here is request-side prefix caching — just local to the customer. No cross-tenant sharing. For hosted we provision isolated KV per customer and TTLs you control.
[02:42] Ally: On compliance — we need to see SOC2 Type II and encryption at-rest keys via our KMS. Also need audit logs shipped to our SIEM. Does Redwood support that across hosting modes?
[02:53] Lena: Yes — hosted supports audit log forwarding and customer-managed KMS integration in our enterprise tier; Dedicated and Private give you more direct control, including on-prem key wrapping. We'll share the security pack.
[03:04] Priya: Another thing, we have a legal ask about data retention — logs older than 30 days must be purged. Does the hosted tier let us control that?
[03:11] Rita: Yes, retention policy per account is configurable; we'll include that in the doc. For private deployments you of course control retention fully.
[03:18] [04:00] Marcus: OK benchmark plan — week 1: baseline hosted run using your sample traffic to measure p50/p95 and token burn. Week 2: step to dedicated footprint simulation (we can provision a small dedicated pool in our staging), run same workload and compare. Week 3-4: optional private pilot if needed for compliance gating.
[04:20] Tom: How long does a hosted benchmark take to be actionable? We want stable numbers.
[04:26] Marcus: We prefer a 24–48 hour run that includes a mix of peak and off-peak periods to capture caching effects. We also want the rerank batch workload run once or twice to validate throughput under larger batches.
[04:40] Priya: Burn rate is big — can you estimate cost per 1M tokens for each mode? Even rough numbers help.
[04:46] Marcus: Yes. Hosted: rough $8–12 per 1M tokens for mixed generation/embedding + re-rank for your workload profile. Dedicated: cost depends on committed capacity — could be lower unit cost once you amortize GPU a fixed monthly cost; think of a 20–30% reduction at scale. Private: variable — on-prem could be cheapest if you already own hardware, but ops overhead is significant. We'll put concrete numbers in the pricing sheet.
[05:05] Evan: I want to understand tail latency — is there a guaranteed P95 in hosted?
[05:10] Lena: We offer latency SLOs as part of enterprise contracts for dedicated pools; hosted has regional performance targets and fallback tiers with documented p50/p95 profiles; exact contractual SLOs are available on our dedicated/enterprise quotes.
[05:23] [07:00] Marcus: Some practical knobs you can use: batching policy (max batch latency), cache TTLs, quantization profile (8-bit vs 4-bit), and fallback model variants for cost/latency tradeoffs. We'll propose a settings matrix as part of the POC.
[07:18] Priya: For quantization — we care about quality regressions. Any evaluation metric to tie quantization to quality drop? We have an internal BLEU-like metric and a rerank NDCG goal.
[07:27] Marcus: Yes — we'll run a small eval set to measure NDCG delta and flag regressions. Redwood Optimize will suggest quant profiles with expected QPS/latency gains and predicted QA impact; it's not perfect but a good starting point.
[07:38] Tom: On timeline — you mentioned a 6-week pilot. Can we get milestones?
[07:44] Lena: Proposed: Week 0 (this week) — onboard + share harness. Week 1 — hosted baseline run. Week 2 — dedicated simulation run and initial cost model. Week 3 — analyze results and adjust configs. Week 4-5 — optional private trial or deeper tuning. Week 6 — decision checkpoint and handoff to Prod/infra for roll out.
[07:58] Priya: That fits our planning. Who is accountable for run execution?
[08:03] Marcus: Redwood will run the hosted baseline with your sample data (you provide it). For dedicated simulation we'll provision a staging pool on Redwood Dedicated and coordinate. You'll own any on-prem setup if private is chosen.
[08:13] Evan: For dedicated pool, do we need to approve capacity ahead of time? I want to avoid surprises.
[08:18] Lena: We'll give a recommended footprint and cost estimate for approval before any commit. No surprises — we won't spin up long-lived reserved resources without sign-off.
[08:29] [10:00] Ally: A quick security Q — for hosted, does Redwood allow pushing logs to our SIEM via syslog or S3? We need immutable logs for audit.
[10:08] Rita: Both options. We support forwarding audit events to your S3 bucket or an external syslog endpoint; retention and immutability can be configured.
[10:18] Ally: And KMS — can we use our cloud KMS and have Redwood encrypt with a customer key?
[10:23] Lena: Yes, customer-managed keys supported on enterprise tiers; we'll include a KMS integration checklist.
[10:30] Priya: Edge-case question — if we pick hosted but later need private for a compliance audit, how hard is cutover?
[10:37] Marcus: We design rollouts to be portable. You can pin model versions and configs, and we support migrations. The heavy lift is data plane (VPC peering, KMS keys). With planning we estimate a 4–8 week cutover for a full private migration depending on network approvals.
[10:53] Tom: That's reasonable. Cost sensitivity: if we see hosted 1M token price at $10, that scales to roughly $3M/year at full load. We need to model a growth path and commitments to make sense financially.
[11:06] Marcus: Exactly — one of the POC outputs will be an amortized cost model with sample growth curves and break-even points between hosted vs dedicated.
[11:14] [15:00] Marcus: Operational concerns — retry behavior, throttling, GC pauses on inference nodes for private. If you run private on-prem, we will provide tuned runtime images; you still need to own node maintenance. Dedicated is Redwood-managed so you get predictable throughput and we handle node maintenance.
[15:20] Evan: For traffic shaping, we have a burst buffer in front of the API; during bench runs we can replay production windows to simulate spikes.
[15:28] Marcus: Perfect. That will help capture tail behavior.
[15:35] Priya: How do we evaluate quality drift during quantization? We want automated regression alerts.
[15:41] Marcus: We'll hook your prompt set into Redwood Optimize's eval runner and set regression thresholds. If NDCG drops by X% or a threshold metric fails, you'll get an alert and the system can auto-fallback to a higher-fidelity model variant.
[15:55] Lena: OK last bit — decision rubric. Think of it as three buckets: 1) Compliance-first (Private) 2) Cost-at-scale + control (Dedicated) 3) Speed-to-value + lower ops (Hosted). We'll send a one-page rubric mapping your requirements to these buckets.
[16:12] Priya: That's helpful. Can we see a worked example? For instance you map our SLOs and budget and tell us recommended mode?
[16:18] Marcus: We'll run that after the hosted baseline; initial expectation: start hosted baseline to validate latency and burn. If p95 spikes or compliance blocks you, move to dedicated for the pilot. Private only if legal requires it.
[16:30] Tom: Any dependencies we need to unblock this week? Network approvals, sample data, and contact for infra to set up VPC peering if we go dedicated.
[16:38] Evan: I'll open a ticket for network info and share the egress/IP allowlist.
[16:42] Lena: Great — I'll follow up with the benchmark harness and a checklist.
[16:46] [25:00] Priya: One minor point — rerank job currently runs on GPUs we own. If we offload that to Redwood, how do we preserve cost controls?
[25:07] Marcus: We'll include rate limits, quotaed routes, and token caps per day in the contract. Also telemetry so you can observe burn in real time.
[25:18] Tom: Ok. Any blockers on our side?
[25:23] Priya: Just the sample traffic and legal team to confirm NDA. We'll loop them in.
[25:30] Lena: Perfect. We'll attach a proposed SOW and pricing bands after we run the hosted baseline.
[25:38] Ally: Please include the KMS integration steps and audit log formats so we can review from a compliance standpoint.
[25:44] Rita: Will do.
[25:47] [35:00] Marcus: To close, here's the measurement plan: 1) Hosted baseline with your traffic capture 2) Measure p50/p95, token burn, and cache hit rate 3) Run rerank batch test to determine throughput 4) Produce cost model and recommend hosting mode.
[35:18] Priya: Thanks. That sounds actionable.
[35:22] Lena: Any other questions?
[35:25] Tom: None from me.
[35:26] Evan: All good.
[35:28] Lena: Great — recap of next steps in the follow-up email. Thanks everyone.
[35:33] [56:30] Meeting end

--- End of transcript ---
notes: Benchmarks: hosted baseline then dedicated sim, optional private trial
Success criteria: P50 < 80ms, P95 < 250ms, 99.9% availability, pilot budget <$20k
